explication:
<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a full-stack Docker management panel (“DPanel”)  
   - Purpose: provide a web UI and CLI scripts to manage Docker containers, images, networks, volumes, backups, crons, SSL certificates, registry sync, etc.

2. Main architectural layers (based on file structure)  
   - Frontend: static assets in asset/index.html + asset/static (React, UmiJS, Ant Design)  
   - HTTP/API layer: Go controllers under app/application/http and common/http  
   - Application logic: app/application/logic and common/logic modules  
   - CLI commands: app/ctrl/command (compose, container, store, user), invoked by docker/script/*.yaml  
   - Service layer: common/service (docker SDK, crontab, ACME, storage, SSH, WebSocket, plugin, registry, notice)  
   - Data access layer: common/dao + common/accessor + common/entity (ORM-generated DAOs and option builders)  
   - Infrastructure/config: config.yaml, migrations under common/migrate, Dockerfiles, Makefile  

3. External systems and dependencies  
   - Docker Engine via unix socket (/var/run/docker.sock)  
   - SQL database (models generated by gen-model.yaml)  
   - Nginx reverse proxy (docker/nginx)  
   - ACME service for certificates (common/service/acme)  
   - Optional remote storage via rclone (through plugin or storage service)  
   - Web browser (classic web UI)  
   - CLI scripts scheduled by host crontab or run manually  

4. Diagram components and relationships  
   a. Frontend (Browser)  
      - Sends HTTP/HTTPS → Nginx  
   b. Nginx (Docker container)  
      - Serves static files  
      - Proxies API calls → Go HTTP server  
   c. Go HTTP Server (main.go)  
      - HTTP controllers → application logic → service layer → Docker Engine / DB / ACME / storage / plugin  
      - WebSocket endpoints → push events to front end  
   d. CLI Module (app/ctrl)  
      - Invoked by shell scripts under docker/script  
      - Shares the same service & data layers as the HTTP server  
   e. Service Layer  
      - Docker SDK calls to Docker Engine  
      - Cron job scheduling (wrapper around host crontab or internal scheduler)  
      - ACME for SSL  
      - Plugin loader & executor  
      - SSH and remote storage interactions  
   f. Data Layer  
      - ORM DAOs → SQL database  
      - Migrations manage schema versions  
   g. External Services  
      - Docker Engine  
      - Database (MySQL/PostgreSQL)  
      - Certificate Authority (Let’s Encrypt via ACME)  
      - Remote object storage (via rclone or other plugin)  

5. Architectural patterns and design principles  
   - Layered architecture (Presentation → Application → Service → Data)  
   - MVC-like controllers for HTTP and CLI adapters  
   - Hexagonal/Ports & Adapters: services encapsulate external dependencies (Docker, DB, SSH, WebSocket)  
   - Reuse of core logic across HTTP and CLI interfaces  

6. Tailoring the diagram for this full-stack web application  
   - Draw two “entry points”: Browser UI and CLI scripts  
   - Emphasize separation: Frontend (React UmiJS) vs Backend (Go monolith)  
   - Show Nginx as the edge component for HTTP routing/static serving  
   - Highlight API layer (controllers) and business logic (services)  
   - Map out data flow: API request → controller → logic → service calls → Docker/DB/etc → response back  
   - Include background tasks: cron scripts → CLI module → same service layer  
   - Annotate key frameworks: Go, Docker SDK, UmiJS/React, Ant Design, ORM  

7. Diagramming guidelines  
   - Use clear component boxes: Frontend, Nginx, Go API, CLI Adapters, Service Layer, Data Layer, External Services  
   - Label each box with its directory or module name (e.g., common/service/docker, app/application/http/controller)  
   - Draw directional arrows for data flow and dependencies (e.g., Go API → Docker Engine)  
   - Color-code by layer: 
     * Frontend (blue)  
     * Reverse proxy (orange)  
     * Backend/API (green)  
     * Service & infrastructure (grey)  
     * External systems (purple)  
   - Use different shapes if desired (e.g., cylinders for DB, clouds for external services)  
   - Include a legend for shapes/colors  

8. Essential details to capture  
   - Dual interfaces (HTTP + CLI) sharing the same core  
   - Docker Engine integration via unix socket  
   - Database persistence (common/dao) and migrations  
   - Plugin system and built-in scripts (docker/script)  
   - Certificate management (ACME)  
   - WebSocket events channel (common/service/ws)  

By breaking the system into these components and showing their interactions, you will create a detailed, accurate architecture diagram that reflects DPanel’s layered monolithic design, its dual HTTP/CLI interfaces, and its integrations with Docker, the database, ACME, and remote storage.
